title: AutoSchema: Self-Prompted Schema Induction and Evidence-Grounded Extraction for Materials Science Literature

problem.claim: Materials science papers contain experimental details needed for structured databases and downstream analysis, but large-scale structured extraction remains difficult.

gap.claim: Existing rule-based and LLM-based approaches can depend on brittle patterns or manually designed schemas, leaving scalable literature mining under schema uncertainty insufficiently addressed.

contributions.claim: AutoSchema bootstraps retrieval and schema induction from a small set of seed papers, iteratively refines the schemas, and freezes them for scalable reuse.
The pipeline performs schema-conditioned, evidence-grounded extraction and produces JSONL audit logs and flattened tables.
The pipeline is applied to a COF literature-mining case study and piloted on additional domains.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across five independent seed sets, canonicalization and semantic normalization increased mean pairwise Jaccard similarity from 19.97% to 43.41% and field-level overlap from 32.50% to 59.91%.
In the COF case study, Phase I expanded the literature to 1,656 papers and Phase II applied the frozen schema to a 200-paper sample.

Compared with ChemDataExtractor and an evidence-grounded ChatExtract-style baseline, the authors report improved coverage, verifiability, and evidence support, while fixed-field prompting can achieve higher fill rate and domain-specific coverage when the target schema is known.

narrative_sequence.summary: Materials science extraction requires experimental details for structured databases, but large-scale extraction is difficult.
Rule-based and recent LLM-based systems are limited by brittle patterns or manually designed schemas.
AutoSchema induces, refines, stabilizes, and reuses schemas while performing evidence-grounded extraction with audit outputs.
The authors report improved schema agreement and describe a COF corpus expansion and frozen-schema sample.
The abstract reports baseline comparisons and additional pilots in other domains, while retaining COF as the main benchmark.

source_observation.claim: The pipeline induces and stabilizes schemas before applying them at scale.

interpretation.claim: Separating schema discovery from frozen-schema extraction may make large-scale extraction more consistent and auditable.

application.claim: For domains with uncertain target fields, use seed documents to induce a compact schema, refine it across rounds, then freeze and audit it during extraction.

exception.claim: When the target schema is already known, fixed-field prompting may provide higher fill rate and domain-specific coverage.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the retrieval sources, schema-induction procedure, or refinement criteria.
The abstract does not provide detailed evaluation protocols, statistical uncertainty, or error analyses.
